analysis: Both changed files are documentation only. docs/developer/serving-performance-qualification.md updates the date and, at head lines 15-22, adds prose on deadline admission estimator corrections (DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES). It says a request with a reviewed calibration keeps the per-row decode charge, at the configured MTP width, in both its calibrated conversion and its fallback. It also says no timing-catalog entry is needed. docs/developer/test.md adds a 'Deadline Admission Estimators' section (head lines 113-138) describing synthetic unit suites (EngineMeasurementOrderingTests, AdmissionRateEstimatorTests, CBv2PerBatchDecode*) and the swift test commands. The patches change no source code, no wire protocol, and no key, attestation, cache-storage, authorization or encryption behavior. The docs explicitly say the tests use scripted engines and synthetic usage and do not qualify live refusal rates, hardware performance or routing. No threat-model assets, trust boundaries or mitigations (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, T-041, T-053/T-054) are weakened or contradicted. The deadline catalog is still stated as empty and profile promotion still requires independent qualification. Open question for later passes: the referenced estimator code (EngineV2Bridge, inference.md#deadlines) is not in this batch, so the docs' behavioral claims about the admission estimator are unverified. They are admission and availability heuristics, not authorization controls, and are not a confirmed security regression.
